head: 558955582fc1
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: completed: retry after an earlier install refused by tailscale up (echoes key) while installer exits 0 (reproduced); auth key as sudo argument (source + partial run); test gaps and docs drift in Optional notes; overlapping PRs #9124, #12815, #8534, #9234

leads.summary: An installed hosted Tailscale connection cannot be switched to Headscale by re-running this installer
leads.consequence: The menu disables Install > Service > Tailscale as soon as the package exists. A direct rerun against a currently Running hosted connection passes the new --login-server but not --force-reauth; Tailscale rejects a ControlURL change (or first rejects an omitted non-default setting such as a previously set operator). The script carries on to enable the receiver and bar and, for an unset admin URL, announces it skipped the hosted web app. The old connection is not migrated. An explicit logout/new profile or documented reauth flow is required; blindly adding --force-reauth may have security/session consequences.

leads.summary: A failed join with an invalid pre-auth key is reported as a completed install
leads.consequence: A real tailscale up failure does not terminate this script. It still attempts operator setup, enables Taildrop and the panel, and may install a web app; the trailing webapp or skip echo returns zero. The menu presentation consequently says Done rather than Failed despite the join error. Open PR #9124 proposes set -e, but merging it with this PR requires manually resolving a conflict near the top of this script; preserve the error handling when doing so.

leads.summary: The pre-auth key is placed in command-line arguments and the test's call log
leads.consequence: Using a literal key passes it to sudo and tailscale as --auth-key=SECRET, exposing it to command-argument observers and any sudo command logging while these processes exist. The new test intentionally writes that argument to its calls file, under its private mktemp directory until its EXIT cleanup; stdout/stderr assertions do not cover these channels. Upstream supports --auth-key=file:/path, which passes a file reference instead of the raw key. Do not characterize 'not printed to stdout' as secret-safe.

leads.summary: The login-server-only input still waits for interactive authentication
leads.consequence: With a fresh daemon and self-hosted login URL but no key, tailscale up starts interactive login, prints an authorization URL and waits for Running without a timeout. The installer cannot reach operator, Taildrop or plugin setup until someone authenticates or interrupts it. Its test's sudo stub unconditionally succeeds, so the 'self-hosted install succeeds' assertion does not exercise the no-auth-key case described as nonblocking in the PR.

leads.summary: The custom admin URL conflicts in behavior with open PR #9234's panel shortcut
leads.consequence: If both non-stacked PRs merge, configuring LOGIN_SERVER=https://headscale.example.com and ADMIN_URL=https://headscale.example.com/admin installs a launcher for /admin, but #9234's panel mark opens https://headscale.example.com instead. A Headscale deployment may not serve a console at the control-plane root. There are no textual conflicts and both suites pass; neither tests the combined custom URL. Feed the configured admin URL to the panel, or have its shortcut open the installed launcher.

leads.summary: A previous hosted web app remains after a direct self-hosted re-install without ADMIN_URL
leads.consequence: On a machine with Tailscale.desktop left from the hosted install, the new self-hosted skip branch only prints a message and never removes that desktop entry. If the user changes the daemon connection out of band and invokes this installer again, the old launcher still points at login.tailscale.com/admin/machines despite the message claiming it was skipped. Menu re-entry is disabled when the package is installed, so this applies to direct invocation; remove or replace the old owned launcher on transition without deleting unrelated user files.

leads.summary: The new URL validator accepts authorities without a host or valid port
leads.consequence: The regex matches https://@ (empty host after a userinfo separator) and https://host:bad (non-numeric port). Such malformed inputs pass all three pre-install checks; package installation and tailscaled enabling happen before the CLI can reject or fail to reach them, contrary to the bad-URL-before-side-effects premise. It also permits userinfo, including passwords which the script echoes as the coordination server. Validate a parsed scheme, nonempty hostname and port (and redact credentials if accepted) before any side effect.

leads.summary: The invalid-input test passes even if package installation moves ahead of validation
leads.consequence: The tests check that sudo tailscale was not called for invalid login server or key, but never assert that omarchy-pkg-add and systemctl were not called. A mutant that installs the package before loading or validating any input passes all six tests, despite breaking the PR's pre-side-effects guarantee. Require an empty call_log (or check absence of pkg-add and systemctl) for every invalid case, and exercise invalid ADMIN_URL too.

leads.summary: This PR conflicts with #9124 and #12815 at the Tailscale installer prologue
leads.consequence: Both open PRs insert a guard at the beginning of the previous short installer (#9124 set -e, #12815 a root-user refusal). Their changes and this PR's new long validation block occupy the same hunk. A three-way merge against each PR's own comparison merge base yields conflict markers before the package call, so a resolver must keep both the new validation and the guards. GitHub lists each as MERGEABLE against the current base independently, which does not answer whether they merge with this PR. #8534's change from $USER to id -un merges without conflicts and should also be preserved.

leads.summary: End-user networking documentation promises a web app even when the installer deliberately skips it
leads.consequence: These entries tell users the menu always installs the hosted admin web app, and contain no way to configure the new self-hosted login server, auth key and optional admin URL. For Headscale without ADMIN_URL, the installer now skips the app. Clarify the hosted default, document a safe direct invocation or session-environment setup for self-hosted installs, and explain the no-admin-URL behavior. The command metadata summary also promises a web app unconditionally.

limits: Current Arch packaging is v1.102.4 (arch-tailscale-package/PKGBUILD:5-17) and its upstream source was checked at that version. The exact package version installed on 2026-09-20 or on any particular user's machine is not known; version-specific behavior should be checked against that user's installed binary if older.

No tailnet, sudo, systemd or desktop was started; sandboxed stubs and source inspection only. The #9234 merged QML integration was source-reviewed, with its pure URL mapper executed; the graphical click was not exercised.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A retry with the new variables after an earlier install fails at `tailscale up`, yet the installer exits 0.

### A retry is refused, echoes the key and reports success

After a run reaches `sudo tailscale set --operator="$USER"`, a later `sudo tailscale up` like the installer's fails ("requires mentioning all non-default flags") because sudo resets `USER`; with a key set, the error prints `--auth-key=<key>`. The script ignores the failure and exits 0. **Impact:** the likely recovery from the reported hang does not join the server: an interrupted menu install still reaches the operator step (simulated), and the menu row is disabled once installed, so the retry comes from a terminal.

**Suggested change:** add `--operator="$USER"` to `up_args`, stop with `sudo tailscale up "${up_args[@]}" || exit 1`, and update the test's exact-match `tailscale up` lines.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 55895558)</summary>

### Reproducer: retrying with the new variables after an earlier run

Two parts. Part A uses the real `tailscale` CLI against a throwaway userspace `tailscaled`. Part B is a test case in the style of `test/shell.d/tailscale-install-test.sh` that fails at 558955582fc1393d4489d8a6596490ff1ec28033.

**Part A: the `tailscale up` command the PR builds, on a node where the installer already reached `tailscale set --operator`**

Needs no root, uses temporary state and a private socket, turns log upload off, and points at `.invalid` control servers, so it cannot join anything. `env USER=root` stands in for `sudo`, which resets `USER` to the target user. Run with tailscale 1.102.3 (`cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go` is identical in 1.102.4, the current Arch package), in an isolated sandbox with no network and `USER=nobody`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
work=$(mktemp -d)
sock="$work/tailscaled.sock"
tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking --no-logs-no-support --port=0 \
  --statedir="$work/state" --socket="$sock" >"$work/tailscaled.log" 2>&1 &
daemon=$!
until tailscale --socket="$sock" status --json >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 0.1; done

as_sudo() { env USER=root tailscale --socket="$sock" "$@"; }

# 1. The first run: `tailscale up` never completes (here it times out; on the
#    menu install it is interrupted at the login URL), then the installer
#    carries on to its operator step.
as_sudo up --accept-routes --login-server=https://first.invalid --timeout=3s
as_sudo set --operator="$USER"

# 2. The retry, with OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_LOGIN_SERVER=https://headscale.invalid and
#    OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY=tskey-auth-EXAMPLEKEY: the command the PR builds.
as_sudo up --accept-routes --login-server=https://headscale.invalid --auth-key=tskey-auth-EXAMPLEKEY
echo "tailscale up exit status: $?"

kill "$daemon"
wait "$daemon" 2>/dev/null
rm -rf "$work"
```

Actual output:

```
timeout waiting for Tailscale service to enter a Running state; check health with "tailscale status"
Error: changing settings via 'tailscale up' requires mentioning all
non-default flags. To proceed, either re-run your command with --reset or
use the command below to explicitly mention the current value of
all non-default settings:

	tailscale up --accept-routes --auth-key=tskey-auth-EXAMPLEKEY --login-server=https://headscale.invalid --operator=nobody

tailscale up exit status: 1
```

A second script ran the same steps with step 1 replaced by the unchanged hosted menu command (`as_sudo up --accept-routes --timeout=3s`, default control URL, no network), printed the node state, and then retried once more with `--operator="$USER" --timeout=3s` added. Actual output:

```
== hosted first run (menu command)
timeout waiting for Tailscale service to enter a Running state; check health with "tailscale status"
exit=1
== operator step
exit=0
== state
  "BackendState": "NeedsLogin",
	"ControlURL": "https://controlplane.tailscale.com",
	"RouteAll": true,
	"OperatorUser": "nobody",
== retry with the PR's variables
Error: changing settings via 'tailscale up' requires mentioning all
non-default flags. To proceed, either re-run your command with --reset or
use the command below to explicitly mention the current value of
all non-default settings:

	tailscale up --accept-routes --auth-key=tskey-auth-EXAMPLEKEY --login-server=https://headscale.invalid --operator=nobody

exit=1
== retry with --operator added
timeout waiting for Tailscale service to enter a Running state; check health with "tailscale status"
exit=1
	"ControlURL": "https://headscale.invalid",
	"OperatorUser": "nobody",
```

With `--operator` named, the settings check passes and the control URL switches; the timeout is only the unreachable `.invalid` server.

**Part B: the installer ignores a failed `tailscale up`**

Change the `sudo` stub in `test/shell.d/tailscale-install-test.sh` to:

```bash
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'sudo %s\n' "$*" >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_CALL_LOG"
if [[ ${1-} == tailscale && ${2-} == up && -n ${OMARCHY_TEST_FAIL_UP-} ]]; then
  echo "tailscale up failed" >&2
  exit 1
fi
SH
```

and append:

```bash
status=$(OMARCHY_TEST_FAIL_UP=1 run_install "https://headscale.example.com" "tskey-auth-secret")
[[ $status != 0 ]] || fail "a failed tailscale up fails the install" "$(cat "$call_log")"
pass "a failed tailscale up fails the install"
```

Actual output at 558955582fc1393d4489d8a6596490ff1ec28033 (the sandbox had no `USER`, hence the empty `--operator=`):

```
ok - hosted Tailscale install is unchanged
ok - self-hosted install joins the given server and skips the hosted admin web app
ok - pre-auth key and custom admin URL are honored without printing the key
ok - a hosted pre-auth key does not drop the admin web app
ok - a login server that is not an http(s) URL is rejected before install
ok - an auth key containing whitespace is rejected
pkg-add tailscale
sudo systemctl enable --now tailscaled.service
sudo tailscale up --accept-routes --login-server=https://headscale.example.com --auth-key=tskey-auth-secret
sudo tailscale set --operator=
systemctl --user enable --now omarchy-tailscale-receive.service
plugin omarchy.tailscale
not ok - a failed tailscale up fails the install
```

With `sudo tailscale up "${up_args[@]}" || exit 1` in the script, the same test file passes.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### The auth key is a `sudo` argument

The key is visible in the process list while `tailscale up` runs, and sudo's default `log_allowed` writes every argument to the system journal (from sudo 1.9.17p2 source, not executed). **Impact:** "is not printed" holds only for the script's own output.

**Suggested change:** pass `--auth-key=file:<path>` from a root-only temporary file (untested end to end), or narrow the description.

**Reproducer:**

### Reproducer: where the auth key ends up

- **Command line.** The PR's own test asserts it (line 76 of `test/shell.d/tailscale-install-test.sh`): the key is an argument to `sudo`, and so to `tailscale`, for as long as `tailscale up` runs:

  ```bash
  grep -Fx 'sudo tailscale up --accept-routes --login-server=https://headscale.example.com --auth-key=tskey-auth-secret' "$call_log" >/dev/null || fail "auth key is passed as one argument" "$(cat "$call_log")"
  ```

  That test passes at 558955582fc1393d4489d8a6596490ff1ec28033.
- **Printed by tailscale on a retry.** See the first reproducer (retry refusal), part A: the refusal prints `--auth-key=tskey-auth-EXAMPLEKEY` to stderr. With `--auth-key=file:<path>` instead, the same refusal printed the path:

  ```
  	tailscale up --accept-routes --auth-key=file:/tmp/tmp.NpkTcFaB3a/key --login-server=https://headscale.invalid --timeout=3s --operator=nobody
  ```

- **sudo's log.** Not reproduced (sudo cannot run in the isolated sandbox). From sudo 1.9.17p2 source, the version in Arch: `log_allowed` defaults to on (`plugins/sudoers/defaults.c`, `def_log_allowed = true`), and each log line carries `COMMAND=` followed by every argument (`lib/eventlog/eventlog.c`, `new_logline`). Omarchy's `etc/sudoers.d` does not change this.
- The userspace `tailscaled` log from the same run did not contain the key (0 matches).
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- With the variables unset or empty, the calls and web app match the merge-base script.
- Every rejected value exits 1 before `omarchy-pkg-add` or any other side effect.
- `--login-server=` and `--auth-key=` are the right forms for tailscale 1.102.x; a key such as `--reset` stays inside `--auth-key=`.
- The new test passes at the head and fails with the merge-base script.
- `bin-style-test.sh`, `tailscale-test.sh` and `installed-service-test.sh` pass at the head.

**Optional notes:**
- Four changes to the script leave the new test at 6/6 `ok`: validation moved after `omarchy-pkg-add`, the admin URL check removed, the admin URL ignored without a login server, and the key echoed on the hosted path. Line 71 (`! grep -F 'secret-auth-key' ...`) can never fail under `set -e`. The tightened assertions below catch all four and pass at the head.
- `manual/35-networking.md` and the `omarchy:summary` line still say the install always adds the admin web app, and only script comments name the variables. The menu can pass them only through the session environment.
- A node already `Running` on another server also needs `--force-reauth` to switch (`cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go`).

### Reproducer: changes the new test does not catch

Each change below was applied to `bin/omarchy-install-service-tailscale` at 558955582fc1393d4489d8a6596490ff1ec28033, and the PR's unchanged `test/shell.d/tailscale-install-test.sh` was run with `bash`. Every run exits 0 with the same six `ok` lines:

```
ok - hosted Tailscale install is unchanged
ok - self-hosted install joins the given server and skips the hosted admin web app
ok - pre-auth key and custom admin URL are honored without printing the key
ok - a hosted pre-auth key does not drop the admin web app
ok - a login server that is not an http(s) URL is rejected before install
ok - an auth key containing whitespace is rejected
```

1. Validation moved after the package install (the description says a bad value exits before `omarchy-pkg-add`):

```diff
@@ -20,6 +20,10 @@
   [[ $1 =~ ^https?://[^[:space:]/?#]+(/[^[:space:]]*)?$ ]]
 }
 
+
+echo -e "\nInstalling Tailscale..."
+omarchy-pkg-add tailscale
+
 if [[ -n $login_server ]] && ! valid_http_url "$login_server"; then
   echo "OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_LOGIN_SERVER must be an http(s) URL, for example https://headscale.example.com." >&2
   exit 1
@@ -35,9 +39,6 @@
   exit 1
 fi
 
-echo -e "\nInstalling Tailscale..."
-omarchy-pkg-add tailscale
-
 echo -e "\nStarting Tailscale..."
 sudo systemctl enable --now tailscaled.service
 
```

(Moving it after `sudo systemctl enable --now tailscaled.service` also passes.)

2. `OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_ADMIN_URL` validation removed:

```diff
@@ -30,10 +30,6 @@
   exit 1
 fi
 
-if [[ -n $admin_url ]] && ! valid_http_url "$admin_url"; then
-  echo "OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_ADMIN_URL must be an http(s) URL." >&2
-  exit 1
-fi
 
 echo -e "\nInstalling Tailscale..."
 omarchy-pkg-add tailscale
```

3. The key printed on the hosted path:

```diff
@@ -49,6 +49,7 @@
 if [[ -n $auth_key ]]; then
   up_args+=(--auth-key="$auth_key")
 fi
+[[ -z $login_server && -n $auth_key ]] && echo "Joining with key $auth_key"
 sudo tailscale up "${up_args[@]}"
 
 echo -e "\nAllowing $USER to manage Tailscale..."
```

4. The admin URL ignored unless a login server is also set:

```diff
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@
 echo -e "\nAdding Tailscale to the bar..."
 omarchy-plugin-enable omarchy.tailscale
 
-if [[ -n $admin_url ]]; then
+if [[ -n $admin_url && -n $login_server ]]; then
   omarchy-webapp-install "Tailscale" "$admin_url" "$admin_icon"
 elif [[ -z $login_server ]]; then
   omarchy-webapp-install "Tailscale" "https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines" "$admin_icon"
```

5. Line 71 of the test, `! grep -F 'secret-auth-key' "$stdout_log" >/dev/null`, cannot fail: Bash's `set -e` ignores a pipeline that starts with `!`, and no case passes `secret-auth-key`. Adding `echo "secret-auth-key"` before `echo -e "\nInstalling Tailscale..."` in the script also passes. The `set -e` part on its own:

```bash
bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; ! grep -F x <<<"x" >/dev/null; echo "reached after a failing ! grep line"'
```

Actual output (exit 0):

```
reached after a failing ! grep line
```

**Tightened assertions that catch 1 to 4.** Against the PR's test file: delete line 71; in the two rejection cases replace the `grep -F 'sudo tailscale' ... && fail` lines with `[[ ! -s $call_log ]] || fail "... is rejected before anything is installed" "$(cat "$call_log")"`; in the hosted auth-key case add `! grep -F 'tskey-auth-hosted' "$stdout_log" "$stderr_log" >/dev/null || fail "hosted auth key was printed" "$(cat "$stdout_log" "$stderr_log")"`; and append:

```bash
status=$(run_install "" "" "admin.example.com")
[[ $status != 0 ]] || fail "an admin URL without a scheme is rejected"
[[ ! -s $call_log ]] || fail "invalid admin URL is rejected before anything is installed" "$(cat "$call_log")"
pass "an admin URL that is not an http(s) URL is rejected before install"

status=$(run_install "" "" "https://admin.example.com")
[[ $status == 0 ]] || fail "hosted install with an admin URL succeeds" "$(cat "$stderr_log")"
grep -Fx 'sudo tailscale up --accept-routes' "$call_log" >/dev/null || fail "admin URL alone keeps the hosted join" "$(cat "$call_log")"
grep -F 'webapp Tailscale https://admin.example.com ' "$call_log" >/dev/null || fail "admin URL is used without a login server" "$(cat "$call_log")"
pass "an admin URL alone replaces the hosted admin web app"
```

Actual results: the tightened file passes at 558955582fc1393d4489d8a6596490ff1ec28033, and fails on each change above with, in order:

```
not ok - invalid login server is rejected before anything is installed
not ok - an admin URL without a scheme is rejected
not ok - hosted auth key was printed
not ok - admin URL is used without a login server
```

**Overlapping open PRs:**
- #9124 (`set -e` in service installers) and #12815 (refuse to run as root) conflict textually with this PR at the lines after the header. #9124 would also stop the script on a failed `tailscale up`.
- #8534 (operator from `id -un`) merges cleanly; the suggested `--operator` should use the same user source.
- #9234 opens the admin console at the daemon's control URL, not `OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_ADMIN_URL`, so with both merged the panel and the web app can point at different addresses.
</details>
